content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name]. I'm trying to figure out how to work with [product_name] Web Editor and have a program running on AWS to control the [product_name] using a smartphone. So far, I have it working - I made a basic program to test managing inputs and outputs. Inputs are functioning properly; I can see their status on my smartphone, although there's some delay, which is acceptable. However, I can't seem to control my outputs. I've set up a button in the AWS app to control the output Q1, but it doesn't respond. I've created a simple program in [product_name] Soft Comfort with one input and one output (I1 and Q1). I added I1 and Q1 to the cloud data transfer settings and marked Q1 as writeable. Then, I went into [product_name] Web Editor to make buttons for I1 and Q1. Using the physical switch for I1 works and is reflected in the app, but pressing the virtual button for Q1 doesn’t have any effect. What could I be missing?

You cannot switch a physical input (I) through [product_name] Web Editor; that's not possible. To achieve what you want, you need to program a network input or a marker (M) in parallel with the physical input (I).

It works, thanks! The only issue now is the delay. When I press the button on the smartphone, it keeps the marker active for about 5 seconds, which causes problems with the rest of the program. Is there a way to reduce this delay or make the button press act as a pulse? Or do I need to assign an on-timer to every marker and set it to around one second?
I can't advise further without knowing which method you are using: switch or button?

analysis.insight_summary: Users can remotely control [product_name] outputs via AWS and smartphones using [product_name] Web Editor, but there is confusion about interacting with hardware inputs versus network markers and virtual buttons. Initial difficulties mainly involve understanding how [product_name] Web Editor communicates with physical and network elements. After clarification, users encounter issues with response delays and need for improved pulse-type functionality rather than sustained signals.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to manage both inputs and outputs on their [product_name] device through [product_name] Web Editor with minimal lag, using simple virtual controls akin to hardware switches. They also look for straightforward configuration steps to distinguish between hardware and network signals.
